jobs.title: Drift Wood #28 · the Rain, ii
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; GULLY — aged 20, stocky boy with a round face, backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie with his hands in the front pocket, muddy tan work boots, easy slouch. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: January again. Wood tries to explain rain to Gully. Gully explains it back. Panel 1: two teenagers sheltering under a shingle shack's eave at a boat launch in torrential January rain drawn as dense vertical hatching, one holding a thermos, black and white (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD). Wood says "Ozu would have held this shot for two minutes. No cut. Just rain.". Panel 2: close-up of a boy in a backwards cap drinking from a thermos under an eave in the rain (in this panel: GULLY). Gully says "Who's Ozu.". Wood says "A Japanese director who understood that nothing happening is something happening.". Panel 3: a boy in a backwards cap nodding out at heavy rain from under an eave, a thermos in his hand (in this panel: GULLY). Gully says "Rain's not nothing. Rain's the river coming up and the crab coming in and the road going out at milepost six.". Panel 4: a silent wide panel of torrential rain over a boat launch and a dissolving bay, two small figures under a shack's eave, dense vertical hatching, black and white, no words (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
